claims.text: A US court found Google’s search business a monopoly because the company engaged in exclusionary conduct by paying billions of dollars to be set as the default search engine, creating a self-reinforcing loop where defaults lead to scale, data, and quality that protect its market position.[Source: ev-1]
Judge Amit Mehta ruled on August 5, 2024 [Source: ev-1], that Google violated Section 2 of the Sherman Act through these default-distribution deals with partners like Apple, Samsung, and Mozilla.
claims.flag: open question: not judgeable from the evidence

claims.text: Evidence showed Google paid approximately $26.3 billion for distribution in 2021 and gave Apple roughly 36% of Safari search-ad revenue [Source: ev-1].
